      HOW TO WRITE TO OUTLET
      ----------------------
Letters are accepted in any form
for publication in OUTLETTERS:
BASIC PRINT or DATA; handwritten
or typed copy; all wordprocessor
files (please state which!) or a
simple JOTTER program is in our
Issue 2(Disk #4).The easiest for
us to edit are Tasword 2 files
with the right margin set at 32.

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From Alan Knight, PENZANCE

Dear Ron/Brian,

I usually run OUTLET on my grey
+2 (in 48K mode, of course). My
present printer is OKI Microline
192 which isn't Epson-compatible
so I've written my own screen
dump routines. Printer interface
is Multiprint from R. Robot. I
may be able to borrow an Epson
compat here, though. I use a
Tandata RGB monitor that "fell
off the back of a lorry" [Ah! so
that's where it went! - B.C.] -
lovely display, pity about the
space it takes up.

Also, I have a Swiftdisk II but
'tis a mixed blessing - the


microdrive emulator is fantastic
but SD is a bit fussy about what
else is on the bus - VTX modem
crashes it and Multiprint is
dodgy too. I usually keep the
last edition of OUTLET on Swift
Disc which works fine under the
emulator.
            - Best wishes

                   Alan

P.S. I just MUST be your most
westerly subscriber - Land's End
3 miles (unless you have a
Scillonian!).

Thanks Alan. Yes, you probably
are the most westerly. Our most
DISTANT subscriber, by the way,
is over 12,000 miles away!-Brian

From: W. Frank Harris, HEXHAM

Dear Ron,

My problem is with my Tasman and
Kempston interface. Once the
Spectrum (48K with 3 x md) has
been in use for some minutes
with the hardware plugged in, my
Tasword 3 program crashes inter-
mittently. I have to write my
letters, store them, disconnect
the Spectrum and leave it for an
hour. Then I can plug in either
interface and, after loading up
the text, print out. Even so,
the program crashes on longish
letters and I waste a lot of
time and paper. The Spectrum
works fine without the hardware
plugged in - I had it serviced
recently.

If you've any suggestions as to
how I can reduce or eliminate
these crashes (both keystroke-
induced and spontaneous, e.g.
whilst the printer is in mid-
page) I'd be grateful. - Frank

I assume by "crash" you mean the
computer no longer responds to
the keyboard or is there another
symptom like a re-set or error
message? Try setting up a long
LPRINT routine in BASIC which,
if it works O.K. would point to
a bug in your Tas 3.Try cleaning
all edge-connectors with a clean
rubber eraser.I personally think
your Spectrum,although otherwise
O.K. can't cope with the load
but what do other readers think?
                         - Brian

From: Alistair McColl,CLYDEBANK


Dear Brian & Ron,

In response to your reply in
Issue 22 re:CAL-PLAN printouts I
give the following info:-There
would appear to be a differance
in the Mannesmann Tally in the
linefeed length so it gives a
printout shorter than the
standard A4 sheet. Now that'S
alright if it's only one page
but when two or more pages are
printed without a break to allow
adjustment things get out of
line with the page perforations.
I enclose the first two or three
sheets of a CAL-PLAN printout as
an example.

The same problem occurs with
OUTPRINT see next paragraph. It
also accurs with commercial
programs that do not allow a
break between pages or allow an
adjustment to be made.

I should perhaps address this to
Mike Haine as it's a problem
with my printer,well not so much
a problem - it's just that I
don't know what to do. How do
you adjust the OUTPRINT program
to give extra skip lines to suit
A4 paper? My printer is a
Mannesman Tally MT80.

        Yours faithfully,

           Alistair McColl.

To: Alistair McColl from Brian

Your printer is normal- it's the
paper which is "non-standard". I
misunderstood you last month! If
you look at adverts for printer
paper, the paper advertised is a
"pseudo A4" (11" in length) and
this is the main standard for
printers but you often also see
a choice of "true A4" which is
just over 11.5" I think. The dip
switches of most printers can be
set to 11"or 12" but not true A4
although I suppose some models
now do so. However, page length
CAN be altered using...

      LPRINT CHR$ 27;"C";N;

       ....where N is the number
of lines per page required.

That line should be included at
the start of printing as it will
set whatever position the paper
is in at the moment as the top
of the paper so set up your
paper first or manually wind it
to the start of a page if you
move it afterwards.

In the case of CAL-PLAN, enter
it into line 9895 just after the
part which says LPRINT CHR$ 27;
"@"; (which initializes the
printer). I have not had time to
test this so you will have to
experiment with the right value
for N but I think it is about 65
to 70 for A4 paper.

CAL-PLAN prints out one page of
the calendar and then sends a

form-feed command to go to the
next page so the above should
work but I don't think OUTPRINT
sends a form-feed - I believe it
is simply calculated to fit a
normal page at the end of which
printers do an automatic form
feed. This means that, although
you can adjust the page length
using the same method as for
CAL-PLAN (the same line 9895)and
the gaps between pages of text
appear correct, the actual flow
of the text will be wrong as it
will still continue text from
column 1 to 2 and 2 to 3 at the
end of a standard-size page if
you see what I mean. Perhaps
Mike Haine can send in some
POKEs to adjust this. What about
it Mike? Any chance?   - Brian

From Les Tyler.

With reference to Grant Dixon's
comments in Issue 21 on the
subject of reversible discs, the
question of possible damage to
discs through their being
rotated in the reverse direction
is an interesting one and ought
certainly to be borne in mind
should problems arise in the
future, as they appear to have
done in Grant's case. However, I
would like to add the following
observations that should also be
considered.

For some years now,Commodore C64
owners with the Commodore single
sided drive have been able to
convert their standard discs to


double-sided capability by the
use of a disc-notcher - readily
available.People of my acquaint-
ance,who have done this,have not
experienced any such problem as
that Grant mentions. One cannot
know, of course, just how much
use the discs of one or the
other have actually had. I found
that I had to have the second
sync hole to operate my discs in
double-sided mode, hence the
acquisition of flippies, and to
date I have not experienced any
problems at all.

Other more knowledgeable
acquaintances tended to poo-pooh
the dislodgement theory, and
thought the problems quoted were
more likely to be due to other
causes.

Only time will tell, of course,
who is right, but to me the crux
of the whole matter is "Do you
want to double your disc
capacity without purchasing new
drives - a considerable expense
for the normal home owner - or
would you prefer to use 2 discs
instead to store the same amount
of information?". ALL floppies
are basically double-sided so
why not use them to the full,
where possible? Flippies are not
really very expensive when you
think of it, consider how many
you can get for the cost of a
double-sided drive, particularly
if,like me,you want dual drives!
Even if Grant's fault does even-
tually arise, it is easily over-
come by a backup disc which one
accepts by default.

On another subject,every now and
then I get the error message:
"Statement Lost"with line/clause
numbers that do not exist. For
some unknown reason this error
message does not seem to be
documented in any publication I
possess or have seen, can anyone
enlighten me as to its purpose?
All the likely alternatives that
occur to me seem to be well-
covered in other error messages.

Concerning SCRABBLE, if anyone
is interested, I have a fully
working conversion of the
earlier 48K program, this gives
all the normal facilities apart
from the SAVE A GAME one. The
conversion is for microdrive
and/or DISCiPLE. Usual load time


on cartridge is about 10-12
seconds - on DISCiPLE about 3.
Call Cheltenham 30784 if you
want further details. I would be
interested to know what the 128K
version has over the 48K one,
should anyone know.

                  - Les Tyler

To: Les Tyler from Brian

Thanks,Les. The "Statement Lost"
message is brought about when
the BASIC interpreter cannot
find the line or statement. Try
entering GO TO 55000! However,if
you use GO TO or GO SUB to a
normal line number between 1 and
9999 which does not exist a ROM
routine corrects this and goes
to the next highest line. This
means you will only normally get
the error message (listed on
p.191 of the original Spectrum
manual incidentally) with a POKE
or machine code crash etc. You
will sometimes see it if you
BREAK into the microdrive
version of OUTLET which uses
FAILSAFE (Issue 6) to detect if

two drives are in use. This also
detects any other errors and, if
so, jumps to line 3000. When a
program is loaded this is
normally switched off at line
8940 but if, for some reason, it
is still operating and you use
BREAK then FAILSAFE will try to
jump to line 3000 which may not
exist in the loaded program -
hence the error message. It is
completely harmless so ignore
it!
                       - Brian.

From: Mike Haine, LEAMINGTON

Dear Ron,Brian & fellow readers,

By now I hope that some of you
will have got my "outprint"
routines going. I know it has
been a long time since I first
described it; I only hope that
it is now worth the wait.

I have to admit that it turned
out to be much more difficult
than"miknet"which prints Prestel
frames in 3 columns (12 to an A4
sheet). That was easier as the
RAM files in which the frames
are stored are well-defined. Of
course, having got it going, I
can see no reason for some of my
stupidities which delayed it so
long.

As Brian says, it still has one
or two little bugs. One he found
is that it won't print a text
file twice without reloading it.
I have found the reason for this
and it can be cured by a simple
addition to the beginning of
line 500. Just insert 'POKE
64951,15 :'. [Have you tested
this, Mike? It did NOT work when
I tried it! - B.C.]

There seems to be a problem with
the Opus intertface. I hope we
can sort that out quickly.

There are lots of things we can
now do with these routines and I
look forward to suggestions? One
possibility I have been toying
with is to arrange to print on

both sides of the paper. This is
obviously possible now but to
get text running continuously
would need some modifications.

Remember the prog will print any
graphics which can be displayed
on the screen so some of the
very nice graphic displays in
the mag could be printed.

It was interesting to see the
comments by Kelvin McWha on
printer dump resolution and by
J.D.Stringer on drawing graphs
on the printer. Both have a
strong relevance to outprint. If
you refer to my article on dmp's
in issue 14 and on, you will see
that the three-column printing
is achieved by first printing

the relevant sections of the
text for the 3 columns onto the
screen.Thus the first 6 lines of
col 1 are in the top 6 lines of
the screen; the first 6 lines of
col 2 next etc. The printer
routine then COPIES line 1 then
prints some spaces, then COPIES
line 6 and ditto line 12. Then
it does same for lines 2,7,13 on
the next printer line and so on.
Thus the full resolution of the
printer page is used in non-stop
printing. Now if the spaces are
left out then the printer can
COPY 120 screen chars. or 3.75
screen lines (twice this in quad
mode!).

Thus a graphic of 3.75 screen
widths and say, 4 screen heights

could be printed on an A4 sheet.
Since a full screen requires 6k
of memory to store it; the full
picture would require 90k. It
could be produced by an ART prog
that allowed appropriate windows
to be displayed on screen and
worked on. I am sure the subse-
quent printing would not require
any very fundamental changes to
the routines used in MIKPRINT
and OUTPRINT.

Full-resolution graphs should be
easier. With an x range up to
960 (1920 in quad density mode).
Let the required function plot
the y values for x o to 255 on
the 1st 6 lines of the screen,
then 256 to 511 on the next 6
and 512 to 767 on next 6 and
rest on last six.

Now the four sections could be
printed across the paper with
very little change to OUTPRINT.
If the calculated y value was
out of the range for the 6 line
region, this would skip to the
next x value. This could produce
some very nice dumps of things
like 3 Dimensional Bessel
functions.....

I hope we shall be getting lots
of response from readers. My
address for anyone who would
like to correspond on prog. or
other Spectrum matters is:-
Mike  Haine,  "Riverside",Welsh
Rd., Offchurch, Leamington. CV33
9AQ. (PRESTEL 788832249).

Thanks, Mike.  -  Brian

To Ian Beeby from Brian

Once more, OUTLET to the rescue!
I have converted minichars 4 for
WORDMASTER use and included it
in this issue. Put your WM cart
or disc in drive 1 and use...

CLEAR 5E3: LOAD*"M";1;"COPY"CODE
     ("COPY" is the Sinclair
     token- enter"THEN COPY"and
     delete the "THEN")

Then LOAD..etc."minicharsW"CODE
from this issue and use...

SAVE..etc."COPY"CODE 54174,11362

      ...on a fresh cart or disc
(leave the original alone until
you know the new version is OK.)

Now transfer the BASIC loader or
type in a new one (see WM manual
p7) and give it a go.

Anyone wishing to design a new
character set for WM note that
each letter is 4 bits wide and
is duplicated at the side thus:-

            XX ww gg

..and should be loaded to 64512.
The WM print routine seems to
wipe out the top line of letters
whether blank or not so leave a
blank line at the top. Existing
Tasword fonts can be converted
with FOR N=ADDR TO ADDR+767:POKE
N, PEEK N + PEEK N*16:NEXT N
which duplicates each 4 bit char
to its left in the byte.

We've ALWAYS accepted OUTLETTERS
in ANY format including Tasword
3 files but I've re-written Page
02 which didn't make that clear.

I regret OUTLET can't cover more
printer interfaces as there just
is not enough room besides which
I don't have the know-how or the
hardware for testing.

Your idea of having instructions
in Tasword files fails our mem-
ory test too (OUTLET text files
are compressed) and anyway they
would have to be IN ADDITION to
our own files as many readers
could not even READ them!However
in your case,as you have Tasword
3, you could use "OUT TO T" from
Issue 22 to create TAS 3 files.
                       - Brian

To: R.W. Jeffs from Brian

You can get more characters per
line on OUTLET print-outs by
using COL80 (Issue 18 - faster
version next month) or OUTPRINT
(#21)which gives 3-column print.

Printing from what I call our
"text mode" (used by OUTLETTERS,
LOOKOUT, etc.) is via a machine
code routine which first has to
decompress the text which has
been encoded to save space. It
then sends each character to the
printer by using the standard
Spectrum ROM LPRINT routines.
This would normally just go to a
ZX-type printer but if the user
has an interface attached it is
diverted to a full-size printer.

Some interfaces may first need
"initializing" and it may also
be necessary to send control
codes to set margins etc. and
this is done from BASIC - in the
case of our "text mode" this is
the CONTENTS BASIC starting at
around lines 1200.Other programs
which include print-out options
have standard routines MERGEd in
- HURRYDUMP(Issue 9)which copies
text only from the screen or we
use a high-res dump on graphics.
Some items just LPRINT strings
of text but ALL need many lines
of BASIC to set up each printer
and interface etc. and this is

To: Alistair McColl from Brian

Your printer is normal- it's the paper which is "non-standard". I misunderstood you last month! If you look at adverts for printer paper, the paper advertised is a "pseudo A4" (11" in length) and this is the main standard for printers but you often also see a choice of "true A4" which is just over 11.5" I think. The dip switches of most printers can be set to 11"or 12" but not true A4 although I suppose some models now do so. However, page length CAN be altered using...

LPRINT CHR$ 27;"C";N;

....where N is the number of lines per page required.

That line should be included at the start of printing as it will set whatever position the paper is in at the moment as the top of the paper so set up your paper first or manually wind it to the start of a page if you move it afterwards.

In the case of CAL-PLAN, enter it into line 9895 just after the part which says LPRINT CHR$ 27; "@"; (which initializes the printer). I have not had time to test this so you will have to experiment with the right value for N but I think it is about 65 to 70 for A4 paper.

CAL-PLAN prints out one page of the calendar and then sends a

form-feed command to go to the next page so the above should work but I don't think OUTPRINT sends a form-feed - I believe it is simply calculated to fit a normal page at the end of which printers do an automatic form feed. Thanks,Les. The "Statement Lost" message is brought about when the BASIC interpreter cannot find the line or statement. Try entering GO TO 55000! However,if you use GO TO or GO SUB to a normal line number between 1 and 9999 which does not exist a ROM routine corrects this and goes to the next highest line. И снова OUTLET спешит на помощь! Я адаптировал minichars 4 для использования в WORDMASTER и включил его в этот номер. Вставьте картридж или диск с WM в дисковод 1 и наберите:

```text
CLEAR 5E3: LOAD*"M";1;"COPY"CODE
```
(«COPY» — это токен Sinclair; наберите «THEN COPY» и сотрите «THEN»).

Затем загрузите `LOAD..etc."minicharsW"CODE` из этого номера и выполните:

```text
SAVE..etc."COPY"CODE 54174,11362
```

...на чистый картридж или диск (оригинал не трогайте, пока не убедитесь, что новая версия работает нормально).

Теперь перенесите BASIC-загрузчик или наберите новый (см. руководство к WM, стр. 7) и пробуйте.

Всем, кто хочет нарисовать свой собственный набор символов для WM: учтите, что каждый символ имеет ширину 4 бита и продублирован сбоку:

```text
XX ww gg
```

...и загружаться должен по адресу 64512. Процедура печати WM, судя по всему, стирает верхнюю строку символов, пустая она или нет, поэтому оставляйте верхнюю строку пустой. Существующие шрифты для Tasword можно конвертировать с помощью:

```text
FOR N=ADDR TO ADDR+767: POKE N, PEEK N + PEEK N*16: NEXT N
```

что продублирует каждый 4-битный символ влево внутри байта.

Печать из того, что я называю нашим «текстовым режимом» (используется в OUTLETTERS, LOOKOUT и т.д.), осуществляется через процедуру на машинном коде, которая сначала должна распаковать текст, закодированный для экономии места. Затем она отправляет каждый символ на принтер, используя стандартные процедуры LPRINT ПЗУ Spectrum. Обычно это работает только с принтером типа ZX, но если у пользователя подключен интерфейс, вывод перенаправляется на полноразмерный принтер.

Некоторые интерфейсы могут сначала потребовать «инициализации», а также может возникнуть необходимость отправки управляющих кодов для установки полей и т.д., и это делается из BASIC — в случае нашего «текстового режима» это CONTENTS BASIC, начинающийся примерно со строк 1200.
